description: Vectors, matrices, and the linear transformations between them: the geometry of many dimensions, and the toolkit under graphics, search, physics, and machine learning.

concepts.title: Linear Algebra
concepts.summary: The mathematics of vectors, matrices, and the transformations between them. Whenever a problem can be approximated by something linear, this is the toolkit, and since almost everything is linear up close, it runs graphics, search engines, and machine learning.

concepts.title: Vectors
concepts.summary: Quantities with both size and direction: a force, a velocity, or simply a list of numbers. Adding them and scaling them are the only operations the whole subject needs, and a vector can stand for a point, an arrow, a pixel, or a document.

concepts.title: Dot Product
concepts.summary: Multiply matching entries and add them up. The result measures how much two vectors point the same way: zero when they are perpendicular, largest when they line up. It is how work, projection, similarity, and angle are computed.

concepts.title: Cross Product
concepts.summary: Given two vectors in space, a third that is perpendicular to both, with a length equal to the area of the parallelogram they span. It gives torque, the normal to a surface, and which way a rotation turns, and it exists only in three dimensions.

concepts.title: Length & Distance
concepts.summary: Ways of measuring a vector's size and the distance between two points. The straight-line length is one; adding up absolute values is another. Choosing the norm chooses what close means, which decides the behavior of everything built on it.

concepts.title: Basis and Span
concepts.summary: A set of vectors from which every vector in a space can be built by scaling and adding, with none of them redundant. Coordinates are just the recipe for a vector in a chosen basis, and switching basis is how hard problems become easy.

concepts.title: Independence
concepts.summary: A set of vectors is independent when none can be built from the others. Independence means each contributes something new, dependence means redundancy, and the count of independent directions is what we mean by the dimension.

concepts.title: Orthogonality
concepts.summary: Perpendicular in the generalized sense: a dot product of zero. Orthogonal directions do not interfere, so problems split cleanly along them. Fourier series, least squares, and principal components all rest on it.

concepts.title: Matrices
concepts.summary: A rectangular grid of numbers that can stand for a transformation, a table of data, or a network of connections. A matrix acts on vectors by multiplying them, and multiplying matrices together composes the transformations.

concepts.title: Matrix Multiplication
concepts.summary: Each entry of the product is a row of one matrix dotted with a column of the other. The rule looks strange until you see it as composing transformations: doing one and then the other. It is not commutative, and doing it fast is a research field.

concepts.title: Determinants
concepts.summary: A single number for a square matrix that says how much it scales area or volume, and whether it flips orientation. Zero means the transformation flattens space, and the matrix cannot be undone.

concepts.title: Inverse Matrices
concepts.summary: The matrix that undoes another: multiply and you get the identity. It exists exactly when the determinant is not zero. In practice one rarely computes an inverse; solving the equations directly is faster and more accurate.

concepts.title: Transpose
concepts.summary: Flip a matrix over its diagonal, so rows become columns. It looks trivial and shows up everywhere: in the dot product as a matrix product, in least squares, and in the symmetric matrices whose nice properties much of physics depends on.

concepts.title: Tensors
concepts.summary: A generalization of vectors and matrices to any number of indices: a grid of numbers with as many axes as needed. In physics they describe stress and spacetime curvature; in machine learning they are the arrays through which data and weights flow.

concepts.title: Linear Maps
concepts.summary: A rule that sends vectors to vectors while keeping addition and scaling intact: straight lines stay straight and the origin stays put. Rotations, stretches, shears, projections, and reflections are all of this kind, and every one is a matrix.

concepts.title: Rotation Matrices
concepts.summary: The matrix that turns every vector by a fixed angle about the origin. It preserves lengths and angles, and its rows are perpendicular unit vectors. Computer graphics, robotics, and spacecraft all rotate things by multiplying by one.

concepts.title: Projections
concepts.summary: Casting a vector's shadow onto a line or plane: the part of it that lies in a chosen direction. Projection is how you find the closest point, and least squares, compression, and dimension reduction are all projections in disguise.

concepts.title: Linear Systems
concepts.summary: Several equations at once, each a weighted sum of the unknowns. They describe balance, circuits, networks, and data fits. A system has one solution, none, or infinitely many, and which one depends on the geometry of the equations.

concepts.title: Gaussian Elimination
concepts.summary: Solve a system by systematically eliminating unknowns, row by row, until it is easy to read off. The method is 2,000 years old, takes about n³ operations, and remains the standard way of solving equations on computers.

concepts.title: Vector Spaces
concepts.summary: Any collection of things that can be added and scaled by numbers, following the familiar rules. Arrows qualify, and so do polynomials, functions, and sound waves, which is why linear algebra applies far outside geometry.

concepts.title: Rank
concepts.summary: The number of independent directions a matrix's output can reach. Full rank means nothing is lost; low rank means the data has less real structure than its size suggests, which is what compression and recommendation systems exploit.

concepts.title: Null Space
concepts.summary: All the inputs a linear transformation squashes to zero. It measures what the transformation forgets. A nonzero null space means different inputs give the same output, so the transformation cannot be undone, and the equations have many solutions.

concepts.title: Eigenvalues
concepts.summary: Special directions a transformation only stretches, never turns, and the stretch factors. They reveal a system's natural modes: the frequencies of a vibrating bridge, the stable state of a Markov chain, the ranking of web pages.

concepts.title: SVD
concepts.summary: Any matrix can be broken into a rotation, a stretch along perpendicular axes, and another rotation. The stretch sizes, the singular values, say which directions matter most. It powers image compression, recommender systems, and noise removal.

concepts.title: PCA
concepts.summary: Find the directions along which data varies most, and describe each point by its position along a few of them. It squashes many measurements into a few informative ones, and is the standard first look at high-dimensional data.
